C.M.A.
 Prayer :

Civil Miscellaneous Appeal filed under Section 173 of the Periyammal vs Lakshmi on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89199870/
1  Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, against the judgment and decree dated  03.06.2009 made in M.C.O.P.No.1336 of 2007 on the file of the Motor  Accidents Claims Tribunal, (Principal District Judge), Salem.
 For Appellants : Mr.R.Nalliyappan  For Respondents : Ms.C.Paranthaman for R2  R1 - died (steps due)
 JUDGMENT

Not being satisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal in M.C.O.P.No.1336 of 2007, the appellants / claimants have come before this Court challenging the same by filing the present civil miscellaneous appeal.

2. The deceased Murugan, aged about 20 years, alleged to be earning a sum of Rs.3,500/- per month, met with an accident on 27.05.2006, when he was travelling in a bus bearing Registration No.TN-30-E-5599, belonging to the first respondent, driven by its driver, in a rash and negligent manner, due to which, the deceased who was standing before the _________ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis front step of the bus, fell down from the bus and he died on the way to the Hospital.

Due to the loss suffered on account of the death of the deceased, the claimants,
who were the parents and sisters, have filed the claim petition.
The said claim petition was resisted by the second respondent / Insurance Company.
3. The claimants have filed the claim petition claiming compensation of a sum of Rs.10,00,000/-.
Before the Tribunal, on the side of the claimants, P.W.1 to P.W.5 were examined and Exs.A1 to A6 were marked.
On the side of the respondents, R.W.1 was examined and no document has been marked and the Court document was marked as Ex.C1.
The Tribunal, after considering the evidence placed on record, had held that, there is negligence on the part of both the bus driver and the deceased.
Hence, the liability has been fixed on the bus driver as well as the deceased equally.
Therefore, the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.1,29,500/- as compensation under various heads and directed the respondents to pay the same jointly and severally to the claimants.
_ _ _ __ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 4.

The learned counsel appearing for the appellants / claimants submitted that, Ex.A5 - AR copy, it clearly establishes that, the deceased fell down from the bus and not jumped from the bus and in order to prove the same, P.W.3 was examined and he also deposed that the deceased fell down from the bus and hence, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the first respondent.

The Tribunal has failed to appreciate the evidence of P.W.5 - ambulance driver wherein he has clearly stated that, he has taken the deceased to the Hospital along with the cleaner of the first respondent.
He further submitted that, the Tribunal failed to appreciate that the minimum monthly income of the deceased, who was aged about 20 years should not be less than that of Rs.4,500/- per month.
Without considering the same, the Tribunal had taken the monthly income of the deceased as Rs.3,000/- which is not acceptable.

Further, the Tribunal considering the entry in Periyammal vs Lakshmi on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89199870/
2

sentences.text: the AR copy and the statement of P.W.4 before the Head Constable-R.W.1, has come to the conclusion that, both the deceased and the bus driver contributed equally for the accident and their liability is fixed in the ratio of 50 : 50, which is unsustainable.
_ _ _ __ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 5.

The learned counsel further submitted that the accident happened in the year 2006 and the at the time of accident, the notional income fixed by the Hon'ble Apex Court is Rs.6,500/- per month, but the Tribunal has fixed the monthly income as Rs.3,000/- which is unsustainable.
That apart, the Tribunal has not arrived at the compensation by adopting proper multiplier in M.C.O.P.No.1336 of 2007.
In fact, the Tribunal has not taken into account the age of the deceased, whereas the Tribunal has taken the age of the parents of the deceased as seen in paragraph No.6 of the award.
The Tribunal has also failed to fix the future prospects.
Therefore, the award itself has been passed by adopting wrong multiplier and also taking the income of the deceased at lesser amount.
6. The first respondent remained ex-parte before the Tribunal.

7. The learned counsel appearing for the second respondent / Insurance Company submitted that even in the FIR, P.W.4, who accompanied along with the deceased had stated that the deceased slept in _________ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis the bus and when the bus proceeded near vellalagundam diversion road, he skipped over the exact bus stop where he has to alighten and suddenly jumped through the front door steps and due to this sudden impact, he caught into the back wheel.
Hence, the accident occurred only due to the carelessness and negligent act of the deceased and the driver or the conductor of the bus is no way responsible for the accident.
Therefore, the second respondent is not liable for the cause of the accident and not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioners.
Even in the AR copy, it is stated that the deceased fell down from the bus.

Considering the entry in the AR Copy and the statement of PW4, the Tribunal has right in coming to the conclusion that both the deceased and the bus driver contributed equally for the accident and their liability is fixed in the ratio of 50 : 50.
8.
This Court gave its careful consideration to the submissions advanced by the learned counsel appearing on either side and perused the materials available on record.
_ _ _ __ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 9.

In order to prove the negligence, this Court perused the evidence of P.W.2 which makes it clear that, if P.W.2 has accompanied the deceased, he would have either lodged the complaint or accompanied the deceased to the hospital.
AR copy entry is the first information about the accident and its contents can be taken as true.
Even in the AR copy, it is stated that the deceased fell down from the bus.
The evidence of P.W.2 that he was travelling with the deceased and the bus was moved while the deceased was alighting lastly, cannot be accepted.
If really P.W.2 was on the spot, he would have taken the injured to the hospital.
Even in the AR copy the name column is filled as 'unknown'.
Therefore, the evidence of ambulance driver that he saw a person lying on the road with injury and he took him to the hospital for treatment is quite reliable.
Therefore, an entry has been made in the AR copy stating that the patient's name as 'unknown'.

Further a perusal of P.W4, makes Periyammal vs Lakshmi on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89199870/
3 it clear that, P.W.4 who accompanied along with the deceased had stated that the deceased slept in the bus and when the bus proceeded near vellalagundam diversion road, he skipped over the exact bus stop where he has to alighten and suddenly jumped through _________ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis the front door steps and due to this sudden impact, he caught into the back wheel.

Considering the entry in the AR copy and the statement of P.W.4 before the Head Constable-R.W.1, the Tribunal has rightly come to the conclusion that both the deceased and the bus driver contributed equally for the accident and their liability is fixed in the ratio of 50 : 50 and hence, this Court also affirm the said view taken by the Tribunal that both the deceased and the bus driver contributed equally for the accident.
10.

Coming to the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, it is seen that the claimants though claimed that the monthly salary of the deceased to be Rs.3,500/-, however, they have not placed any documentary evidence to prove the same.

In such a backdrop, considering the fact that the accident had happened in the year 2006, this Court is inclined to fix the notional income of the deceased at Rs.6,000/- by applying the ratio laid down by the Apex Court in Syed Sadiq & Ors.

Vs.
The Divisional Manager, United India Insurance Co. Ltd (2014 (2) SCC 735).

sentences.text:
, this Court fixes the future prospects at 40% and accordingly arrive at the loss of monthly income to the family at Rs.8,400/- [Rs.6000/- + Rs.2400 (40% of Rs.6,000/-)] .
11. Applying the monthly income at Rs.8,400/- and deducting 50% towards his personal expenses,
the deceased being a bachelor, the loss of monthly income to the family is fixed at Rs.4,200/-
(Rs.8,400/- X 50%).
12.
Further, the Tribunal committed error in not applying the appropriate multiplier in this case.
Having regard to the age of the deceased at the time of his death, i.e., 20 years, the applicable multiplier in terms of Sarla Verma & Others.

Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation & Others (2009 (6)
SCC 121) would be '18'.
Hence, the loss of income would be Rs.4,200/- X 12 X 18 = Rs.9,07,200/-.
_ _ _ __ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 13.

Insofar as the compensation under the head love and affection is concerned, though the Tribunal has awarded Rs.20,000/- as compensation under the said head, this Court is inclined to modify the same to a sum of Rs.40,000/- each to the claimants, i.e., the parents and the sisters of the deceased as per the decision laid down in Pranay Sethi's case.
However, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the head funeral expenses at Rs.5,000/- is very minimal and is not justified.

Hence,
the same is modified as Rs.15,000/-.
Since the Tribunal has not awarded any compensation under the head loss of estate, this Court is inclined to award a sum of Rs.15,000/- under the head loss of estate.

14. In the above circumstances, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the below mentioned heads is modified as under:
